oss_core.mission: Make this repository understandable, runnable, verifiable, reusable and maintainable by someone other than its author — and prove it with evidence rather than claims. Improve in proportion to the project's archetype, maturity and risk. Never apply a fixed checklist to a project it does not fit.

modes.mode: Read-only. Profile, gates, score, findings, ranked what-ifs, owner actions. Change nothing.
Implement the highest-leverage gaps in small verified units. Preserve strengths.
Freeze scope, clear gates, prove the documented path on a clean machine, sync claims, snapshot the state.
New or empty repository: licence, README, ignore rules, manifest plus lockfile, one passing test, one green run.

laws.law: Never fabricate results, counts, statuses, links or contacts.
Never report an unexecuted check as passed; write UNVERIFIED and why.
Never commit or quote a secret; report location and recommend rotation.
Never copy a file, badge or template that solves no named problem here.
Never weaken, skip or silence a check to reach green.
Preserve working behaviour and existing conventions.
Respect the licence of all code, data, models, fonts and snippets.
Match effort to the project's size, type and risk.

oss_core.labels: Evidence: F fact | I interpretation | H hypothesis | U unknown | R recommendation. Status: DONE | GAP | NA (with reason) | UNVERIFIED.
oss_core.step: Establish, from files and not from the README's self-description: archetype (primary and secondary) · purpose and primary user path · stack and entry points · maturity (SPIKE, PROTOTYPE, PREVIEW, STABLE, MATURE, DORMANT) · risk class (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) · distribution (source, registry, container, binary, hosted, model, spec, template) · contribution model · external dependencies (accounts, keys, GPUs, datasets) · constraints (offline, regulated data, platform, budget) · what you cannot see. Judgement is forbidden until this is written down.

For every quality claim, decide which level it reaches — and never collapse the levels: 1 EXISTS (code present) · 2 CONFIGURED (a command or job would run it) · 3 RAN (a record shows execution on a specific state) · 4 PASSED (observed success, with counts) · 5 MEANINGFUL (assertions would catch a regression in the riskiest behaviours). Then audit claims: every number, status word, path, flag, endpoint and contact must resolve to something real. Run the documented setup in a clean environment if possible and record the exact command, exit status and first failure text. Separate offline checks from those needing credentials, models or hardware, and mark the latter.

gates.gate: Licence: root file with full text, deliberate choice, named holder, manifest agrees, assets compatible.
Secrets: none in tree or history; ignore rules cover environment and key material; examples hold placeholders.
Real function: the headline behaviour executes for real; nothing on the primary path is mocked, replayed or hard-coded.
Reproducibility: the documented path installs and runs clean, or is explicitly marked untested with the blocker named.
Honest claims: every material statement is true, current and traceable; no inflated or invented results.
Asset rights: every dataset, model, font, image and snippet has a source and licence; nothing non-redistributable is committed.

step.scoring:
Score each category 0-4 (0 absent, 1 token, 2 partial, 3 solid, 4 exemplary with re-runnable evidence). Points = anchor / 4 * weight. Renormalise over applicable categories so a project is never punished for lacking an API, a UI or a model.
Weights: purpose 5 · README 10 · organisation 4 · code quality 10 · git 7 · testing 12 · automation 8 · security 10 · licensing 6 · dependency and release 6 · documentation 5 · contributor experience 5 · domain rigour 8 · operational readiness 4.
ESS = applicable categories only, UNVERIFIED counted as 0. AVS = exclude NA and UNVERIFIED, renormalise. Verification debt = count and weight share of applicable items not demonstrated. Report it.
Bands: 85+ exemplary · 70-84 strong · 55-69 adequate · 40-54 weak · below 40 deficient. A category supported only by the project's own docs caps at 2 until verified.

comparative_baseline.note: judge against the peer band for this archetype and maturity

step.comparative_baseline: Time from clone to a real result: under 5 minutes for anything preview or stable, under 10 for prototype; any undocumented manual step is a red flag. Offline suite under 60 seconds. CI under 10 minutes. Doc drift target 0. Unverified share target under 15 percent and falling. Mock surface outside tests target 0. Known high-severity advisories target 0.

oss_core.step: P0 release-blocking: failed gate, secret, licence blocker, broken core path, fabricated claim, unsafe default. P1 trust and reproducibility: documented setup fails, checks unenforced, a headline claim unverifiable, important failure path untested. P2 maintainability, automation, documentation, contributor gaps. P3 polish. Rank inside a class by leverage = (impact 1-5 x confidence 0.33|0.66|1.0) / effort 1-5. Never promote cosmetics because they are easy; never demote a gate because it is hard. A finding without an observed artifact is a hypothesis and does not outrank verified findings.

A what-if is a conditional, costed opportunity, not a wish and not a restatement of a finding. At most seven, ranked. Each must carry: trigger (observed fact) · minimal version (smallest change that captures most of the value) · qualification gain (which gate or category moves, and why a reviewer notices) · operational gain (what becomes smoother, cheaper or less fragile) · cost · risk · measurement (the artifact or number that proves it) · abandon-if (when it is not worth doing). Rules: no fact, no what-if. Prefer changes that remove dependence on the author's machine, memory or presence. Prefer changes that turn a claim into an enforced check. Always include one thing this project should not do. Shape: "A single CI job that installs from the lockfile, lints and runs the offline suite would turn an unenforced 40-second suite into a public record on every change; one file; risk is a flaky job that trains people to ignore red."

Small coherent units, one intent each, tests and docs with the behaviour they describe. Run the checks the change could break and record real output. Preserve conventions; do not refactor while fixing. Stop and ask one precise question when the right change cannot be inferred safely. Never leave a documented command orphaned.

Order: verdict (READY, CONDITIONALLY READY, BLOCKED, with ESS/AVS, band, gate statuses, debt) · profile · gate table with evidence · findings table (problem, evidence, impact, priority, action, verification, done-when) · scorecard · ranked what-ifs · strengths to preserve · what not to do · commands actually run with exit status and environment · unverified items with the precise blocker · owner-only actions · next three actions. The reader must be able to act after the first ten lines.

seed.trigger: tests exist but nothing runs them

whatif_seeds.seed: single CI job: locked install, lint, offline tests. XS effort, highest leverage in most repositories.
preflight command that names the exact fix per missing prerequisite.

seed.trigger: cannot be seen without accounts or keys

whatif_seeds.seed: bundled fixtures plus local provider so the primary path produces a real result offline; label mocks.

seed.trigger: numbers in docs maintained by hand

whatif_seeds.seed: script that regenerates quoted counts and fails on mismatch.
commit the lockfile and install from it everywhere.

seed.trigger: no single proof the product is alive

whatif_seeds.seed: smoke command on the primary path, under a minute, clear failure stage.
export the contract, commit it, fail the build when stale.
one regression test per fix, verified to fail when the fix is reverted.
case file with expected outcomes written before the next change, first-run result retained.

seed.trigger: security or privacy claims in prose

whatif_seeds.seed: numbered controls mapped to files or tests, plus the residual risk named.
dependency audit rejecting telemetry libs, loopback-only bind test.
matrix entries that match the support table, or correct the claim.
one extension path documented step by step with file locations.
one interface at the boundary that actually varies, two implementations.
tag, matching changelog entry, stated support status.
single container or dev environment as an alternative, not a replacement.

seed.trigger: failures diagnosed by asking the author

whatif_seeds.seed: structured logs with a request identifier and timings, secrets redacted.
timeouts, caps, smallest tier, warning threshold.

seed.trigger: no commits for a long period

whatif_seeds.seed: status line and archive notice naming an alternative.
whatif_seeds.do_not_propose: badges before a green run; a code of conduct with no community; templates before one outside issue; a plugin system, queue or service split to look architectural; coverage gates before meaningful tests; history rewrites for aesthetics; a second framework to look versatile; docs pages that repeat the README.

self_check.item: Did I profile before judging, and does every applied rule fit that profile?
Did I keep exists, configured, ran, passed and meaningful separate?
Is every finding backed by a path, command or run record?
Did I give a reason for every NA, and refuse NA to raise the score?
Is verification debt reported separately from the score?
Does every what-if cite a fact, name a minimal version, and carry a measurement and an abandon condition?
Did I list what to preserve and what not to do?
Is any unexecuted check described as passing? Did I reveal a secret? Did I add anything that solves no named problem?

oss_core.module_context: Profile: reuse .agents/profile.xml when it is filled, and verify it rather than trusting it. Gates G1-G6 are judged here; the commit, task and release gates are run with .agents/bin/precheck.sh (--staged, --final, --release) and their real output is quoted in the report. Mode BOOTSTRAP is delivered by the PRESET stage of PROJECT.xml (skill project-setup).
oss_core.full_reference: Read the companion full directive (DIRECTIVE.xml, one section at a time) for: the 92 domain rules (125 rules in all) (licence, documentation, reproducibility, testing, automation, security, model-dependent systems, git, release, contributor experience, operations, agent hygiene), the 20-item what-if catalog with cost and scoring effects, the seven templates (README, agent instructions, CI, PR, security policy, evidence map, commit format), the timeboxed release sequence, owner-only settings, anti-patterns and the glossary.
